summary.text: A 51-year-old woman with type 2 DM had poor blood glucose monitoring records and irregular medical treatment before a TVT-O procedure with synthetic sling implantation for urinary incontinence. After endocrinology consultation insulin therapy was initiated and her blood glucose spectrum was stable before the procedure, which was successful without intraoperative or immediate postoperative complications; she was discharged the following day. She failed to comply with glucose monitoring and glibenclamide.

She had been discharged 1 week earlier when she presented to the emergency department with dyspnea, dizziness, severe right thigh soreness and difficulty walking, with a temperature of 37.5°C. Examination showed right inner leg redness and swelling, right vaginal wall tenderness and stench, blood glucose 38.6 mmol/L and white blood cell count 25.79 × 10^(9)/L. Emergency CT showed gas shadows, and DKA and cellulitis were diagnosed.

The abscess was drained by ultrasound-guided puncture, and the drained fluid indicated mixed anaerobic bacterial infection. Once glucose, electrolytes and acid-base balance were controlled, antimicrobial agents were started after Infectious Disease consultation. After multidisciplinary consultations she was advised to continue anti-infective therapy, puncture drainages and close observation. The sling was not removed and no extensive incision was performed.

Cellulitis shrank with DM stabilization and her condition gradually relieved. MRI showed no collection of air bubbles, and she showed complete recovery 4 weeks later. At follow-up visits 3, 6, 12 and 24 months after discharge she maintained urinary continence with well-controlled DM, with no signs of infection, urine leakage or related lower urinary tract symptoms. Pelvic floor ultrasound showed a continuous sling shadow under the mid-urethral area. No sling exposure or erosion was observed.
